Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:123: And therefore I say that whoever has no rooster should seek a companion who does not sleep until midnight, so that he wake him at exactly midnight - and his companion has a reward, as it is written concerning David and his men (1 Samuel 30:24), "for as the share of him who goes down to battle, so shall the share of him who stays by the baggage be; they shall share alike" - and so they should alternate, or he should have a craftsman [companion] who is not particular about the matter. And if he is in a place where none of the preceding options are available, it is fitting that he not lie on a made bed, and not fully undress. And I heard that the sage, his honor Rabbi Yosef Taitatzak, peace be upon him, for seventy years did not sleep on a made bed except from Sabbath to Sabbath, and they said that his custom was to sleep on top of a chest with his legs hanging, and he would rise at exactly midnight, and no one knew of this until after his death, when his wife told of it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:124: And it is fitting to swear an oath and make a vow to fulfill these preparations, for we find that King David, peace be upon him, swore and vowed something similar, as it is said (Psalms 132:2), "who swore to the LORD, vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob: surely I will not come into the tent of my house, nor go up into my bed; I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids," and so on. In any case, he should swear only to something he judges in his mind that he can fulfill. And concerning the conditions of vows and oaths, we wrote below in chapter 14 - see there. And so it is fitting to swear not to indulge in eating and drinking beyond a measure he knows will not increase his sleep.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:125: And if he prepares a rooster, he should strive that it be black, for it is more precisely attuned than others - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 218b), in these words: and therefore, at exactly midnight, when the wind from the north side is aroused, one flame goes out and strikes beneath the wings of the rooster and it calls - and all the more so with a black rooster, which is more precisely attuned than another - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:126: Also, whoever is not accustomed to fasting and not to rising at midnight - it is good for him to eat by day, at least one hour before nightfall, so that there be time for the food to digest and his sleep not increase when he rises at midnight - and he should conduct himself this way for some time until he is established in this measure, especially in the summer days when the nights are short.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:127: Also, it is fitting that he train himself to sleep in some of his clothes, and not sleep naked within the sheets, for it will be hard for him to rise, especially in cold weather - and this is the measure of alacrity, that he be alert before he comes to a stumbling block - for they said (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 4), "this is the way of Torah: sleep on the ground" - the reason being that he should be uncomfortable and not find his body resting so that he come to sleep the whole night, as Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, peace be upon him, explained. And at the very least, if he lacks the strength to sleep on the ground, he should not indulge in sleeping in a made bed with sheets. And all this is fitting for whoever wishes to repent and repair the rest of his nights, so that he not be held accountable for the several nights he lost to sleep and idleness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:128: And according to the words of the Zohar, a person is forever obligated to rise to occupy himself with Torah at night, whether in the rainy season or the summer season, for they said (Parashat Bereshit, page 4a), "who does not anticipate this every day," as we copied above. But at the end of Tractate Ta'anit (31a), whoever does not rise from the fifteenth of Av onward - "whoever adds, is added to; whoever does not add, is gathered in" - and Rashi explains, from this point onward, from the fifteenth of Av onward, whoever adds nights to days to occupy himself with Torah shall add life to his life; whoever does not add to the occupation with Torah, his mother shall bury him, meaning he shall die before his time - to this point. And some have given a mnemonic for the matter: "from my lying down until my rising, lie down" - meaning from Shavuot until the Ninth of Av, lie down [sleep more], since the nights are short; and "from my rising until my lying down, rise" [the rest of the year]. But the essential thing is to fulfill the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, especially for one who wishes to sanctify himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:129: Upon rising at midnight, it is fitting that he suffer in the suffering of the Shechinah, and weep and lament over the destroyed Temple and over His profaned Name, and finally over his own sins that lengthened the exile of the Shechinah - for it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 196a) that at midnight the Holy One, blessed be He, remembers Israel who are in exile and the destruction of His house, and so on, and then the souls of the righteous return to their bodies, and the angels say to them, "behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD," and so on. And midnight is a time of favor, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 173b), fitting for prayer that the Holy One, blessed be He, forgive his sins and restore him to repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:130: Afterward he should rise to occupy himself with Torah, and put on his clothes and prepare himself to meet his God - and so it says in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 72a), in these words: Rabbi Yehudah rose one night to labor in Torah at the guesthouse in the town of Machseya, and there was a certain Jew there. He said to him, how can this matter be, is it not the Foundation Stone, and so on? Rabbi Yehudah did not turn his head toward him. He opened and said (Amos 4:12), "prepare to meet your God, O Israel," and it is written (Deuteronomy 27:9), "be attentive and hear, O Israel" - the words of Torah require intent, and the words of Torah require that the body and the will be prepared together. That Jew arose and dressed and sat before Rabbi Yehudah and said, happy are you, righteous ones, who strive in Torah day and night. Rabbi Yehudah said to him, now that you have prepared yourself, tell your words so that we join together - for the words of Torah require the preparation of the body and the preparation of the heart, and if not, [he said] I would have lain in my bed and spoken the words in my heart. Rather, we have learned that even one who sits alone and labors in Torah, the Shechinah joins with him - so how is the Shechinah here while I lie in my bed? And not only that, but purity is required, and further, everyone who rises to labor in Torah from midnight, when the north wind is aroused at midnight, the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to delight with the righteous in the Garden of Eden, and He and all the righteous in the Garden of Eden heed him, and heed those words that come out of his mouth - and while the Holy One, blessed be He, and all the righteous delight in hearing the words of Torah at this hour, shall I lie in my bed? - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:131: Upon rising he should occupy himself with the Oral Torah or with Mishnah - and so the Targum translated the verse (Lamentations 2:19), "arise, cry out in the night": "Arise, O Shechinah of Israel, who dwells in exile, occupy yourself with Mishnah at night, for the Shechinah of the LORD dwells opposite you." And so it says in the Yalkut, end of Parashat Ki Tisa (siman 406, page 111a), on the verse "and he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights" (Exodus 34:28) - but is it not written (Daniel 2:22), "and light dwells with Him," "and brightness shall be as the light" (Habakkuk 3:4), "even darkness is not dark to You" (Psalms 139:12)? How did Moses know when it was day and when it was night? At the time the Holy One, blessed be He, taught him Scripture, he knew it was day; at the time He taught him Mishnah, he knew it was night - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:132: And it is good that he rise standing, as much as he can bear, so as not to sleep - for so King David, peace be upon him, would do, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 82b), in these words: come and see, King David would rise at midnight - for should you say he would sit or lie on his bed and recite songs and praises - no, rather, as it is written (Psalms 119:62), "at midnight I rise to give thanks to You" - "I rise" certainly means standing, to occupy himself with songs and praises of Torah - to this point. And it is possible that Scripture also intended this in saying "arise [kumi], cry out," namely rising while standing. And at the very least, if he lacks the strength to stand from the beginning of the reading, if sleep comes upon him he should rise and stand - for the essential thing is to bind night with day through the occupation with Torah, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:133: And he should also read his studies aloud, and thereby gain that he not fall asleep and not forget it, as it is said (Proverbs 4:22; cf. Eruvin 54a), "for they are life to those who find them." And concerning the virtue of raising one's voice at the time of study, they elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Shemini, page 39b) on the verse (Song of Songs 7:10), "and your palate like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved" - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:134: And the sum of it all: whoever wishes to be constant in this measure should strive in his deeds to acquire the neshamah - for they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 25a) that whoever merits the neshamah is the one who is strengthened like a lion in the occupation with Torah from midnight to morning, the reason being that the neshamah gives him strength. And we have already explained above (chapter 4) that the neshamah is acquired through the occupation with Torah, and also through the purification of thoughts. Also, it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 113b) that penitents merit an additional soul every day, and therefore it should not be hard for a penitent to rise at midnight, since the soul comes to him from a place called "strength" [ko'ach].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:135: Also, among the things needed to acquire this measure is that a person sanctify himself properly by day, purify his thoughts, and occupy himself with Torah to give satisfaction to his Creator and not for any worldly matter - and through this he removes his soul from "Asiyah" [mere doing] and it cleaves to holiness, and through this he shall merit the neshamah. Now, we already know, as explained in the previous chapters (chapter 4) through the teachings of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that the acquisition of the neshamah is through the occupation with Torah and the purification of thoughts. And in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 141b) it is explained that through the neshamah the Shechinah is aroused to unification, in these words, concerning the neshamah: and this is for whose sake the lamp shines to illuminate above, and it says, through this is included whoever is included, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:136: Now, when a person is engaged in mere doing and does not direct his intent to the One before whom he stands, whose glory fills the whole earth, he is physical and in "Asiyah," and has no neshamah. And so with his eating and his blessings - if he blesses calmly and deliberately, and intends to give praise to his Maker, who is always before him - and this is the intent of "Blessed are You," by the plain meaning - and does not cast the blessing from his mouth in haste; and so with his eating, that he eats as one who eats before the King, and directs his intent in his eating as explained in its place - through this he removes himself from physicality and sanctifies his soul with supernal spirituality, and shall merit the neshamah, and then the Shechinah rests upon him, and since he is at the level of "living," sleep shall not overpower him. But whoever is physical in his ways is in "Asiyah," and sleep, which is death, shall overpower him - would that he merit even the ru'ach.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:137: The second matter that causes the holiness of thought is a person's conduct during the six weekdays properly, as shall be explained, so that on the Sabbath day he receive the holiness of the Sabbath, and the Sabbath find a receptacle in which its holiness may rest - and concerning this the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded us in the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:8), "remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it; six days you shall labor and do all your work, and the seventh day is a Sabbath," and so on. And its explanation is according to what we explained above in this Gate, chapter 2, that all the days nurse from the Sabbath day, as we established there, and there we copied their teaching, of blessed memory (Mechilta, Parashat Yitro), that they said, "remember the Sabbath day" - that you should count toward the Sabbath, as explained there. And the intent is that the holiness of the Sabbath is a very supernal holiness, and it is impossible for a person to attain it because he is clothed in the six weekdays, over which the thirty-nine categories of work rule, and so on, as we elaborated there - and therefore he must sanctify himself every day with the holiness of the Sabbath, so that when the Sabbath day comes he may be able to receive its holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:138: And it is like the parable of a person who is in darkness, who, if he goes out into the light and receives the full strength of the sun's light, would darken his eyes and not enjoy the sweetness of its light - and as the verse says (Hosea 6:3), "and let us know, let us pursue to know the LORD; His going forth is sure as the dawn," for the light of dawn shines little by little - so the light of the holiness of the Sabbath is a supernal holiness of Atzilut that Atika Kadisha illuminates, as Rashbi explained (Parashat Yitro, page 89a), as we elaborated there - and who, who can receive that great holiness?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:139: And it is also a parable to a garment upon which stains of oil and the like have fallen - that if it is not washed and bleached properly, it cannot receive any dye. So one who comes to receive the light of the Sabbath while defiled, his soul soiled with the stains of his sins, has no place for the light of the supernal soul to rest, for it has no place to rest - and therefore one must remember the Sabbath from the first day of the week, so that every single day he sanctify himself, until, when the holiness of the Sabbath comes, the person is already trained in it and it finds a repaired throne to rest upon.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:140: And this is what it says, "remember the Sabbath day" - and the word "zakhor" [remember] is an infinitive, that one must forever remember the holiness of the Sabbath day, "to sanctify it," meaning so that you can sanctify it and receive its holiness, in a manner that when the Sabbath day comes it shall shine upon all the days with strength - for all the days are repaired properly and included in the central point. But if the days are not repaired, and a blemish is found in them, Heaven forfend, the Sabbath will not shine upon them from their side, since they cannot receive its light - and all this is from the side of the soul of this blemishing person; he shall not receive that illumination because he has not repaired [his days]. And this poor person is found lacking in two things: lacking, on the Sabbath day, the holiness of the Sabbath, and lacking, in the coming six days, since the days of the past week did not receive the light of the Sabbath properly, so that they might shine properly in the coming week.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:141: Therefore it is proper on Friday to repent fully and confess everything he blemished during the six days, in order to receive the light of the Sabbath properly, as explained. And it is possible that with this intent a certain rabbi would fast every Sabbath eve. And in saying "the light of the Sabbath," the intent is the additional soul, which each one receives according to the merit of his deeds during the six working days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:142: And therefore Scripture says (Exodus 20:9), "six days you shall labor [ta'avod]," and so on - the explanation being that in order to receive the holiness of the Sabbath, one must labor for six days, meaning that he be at the level of a servant [eved]. And the conditions a servant is obligated to serve his master, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the precepts, printed at the end of Parashat Behar Sinai (page 111b), on the verse "for the children of Israel are servants to Me" (Leviticus 25:55), and we shall not copy all his words so as not to lengthen this, but the conclusion of his words: he said that included in "servant" are two aspects - included in "servant" is prayer, called "service" [avodah], as they said (Ta'anit 2a), "what is the service of the heart? This is prayer" - and included in it is to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, with every kind of service, which are the commandments, like a servant serving his master, because he is commanded to serve Him. And included in this, although Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai did not write it there, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of the Service of God, chapter 5) that among the conditions of a servant is to be careful not to do anything contrary to his master's will - and this is the negative aspect - and he elaborated at length there on the conditions of a servant - see there. And the second aspect in "servant" is the occupation with Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:143: And in each of these one must combine the aspects of son and servant, for Israel is called "servants," as it is said (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me," and is called "children," as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:144: Concerning prayer, one must be both servant and son - servant, to repair what is relevant from the Shechinah downward, in the lower worlds, and to unify in Atzilut, from where they are called sons. And whoever knows what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Pekudei, concerning the order of the palaces, in the blessings of the Shema and in the Amidah prayer, will see that everything is done as one, servant and son. Concerning the occupation with Torah, he said that when a person knows and recognizes his Maker only according to the plain meaning, in general he is called a servant - and so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b), that the six orders of Mishnah are in Metatron, called a servant, and from there come the pure and the impure, and so on, as explained above in chapter 2. And when he is a son - meaning one who knows the secrets of Torah, which are in Atzilut, like a son who searches his father's treasuries - he is called a son. This is the sum of his words there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:145: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Mishpatim, page 115a), they explained the reason that one who occupies himself with Torah is called a servant, and they said, in these words: (Exodus 21:2), "if you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve" - and what is his acquisition? Rather, in the secrets of Torah: Metatron, servant of the LORD, comprises the six directions, corresponding to the six orders of Mishnah, and through them a person must serve his Master, to be a servant sold, "an acquisition of his money" - for money is the right hand of Abraham, Chesed his level, from where the Torah was given - and whoever strives in it in order to merit the World to Come is called "an acquisition of his money," the world of longing [kesufa] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:146: And he said further there, two particulars in which a person is called a servant: the first, in tefillin - he said that he is His servant through the yoke of tefillin on his head, and his ear is opened through the strap to hear the Shema - "hear" in whatever language you understand. And the second aspect, in prayer, as they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 34a), that the first three blessings [of the Amidah] resemble a servant arranging his praise, and so on, and the last three resemble a servant who has received a gift from his master, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:147: Now, Scripture alludes to all these aspects in saying (Exodus 20:9), "six days you shall labor" - for when the days are repaired with these aspects, they shall be a throne to receive the light of the Sabbath.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:148: And now it is fitting to know where in Scripture the aspect of "son" is alluded to, according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who said that a person must always be both servant and son together, whether in prayer or in Torah. And it may be said that it is alluded to in Scripture's "remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it, six days" - and it is known that the Sabbath day, which is the light of Atzilut, is the aspect of "son." And we have already said that "zakhor" [remember] is an infinitive, that one must always remember the aspect of "son," which is the Sabbath day, even during the six days, which is the secret of "servant" - aside from the Sabbath day itself, which is entirely "to the LORD your God." And the prayer of the Sabbath day is not like the prayer of the weekdays, and the occupation with Torah on the Sabbath day is not like its occupation on weekdays - for on weekdays one directs his intent to the six orders of Mishnah in Metatron, and on the Sabbath day he directs them to the six extremities in Atzilut, where their source is, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 106b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:149: And all the holinesses practiced on the Sabbath day - which are the holiness of thought, the holiness of speech, and humility, which we explained above and explained in chapter 2 - one is obligated to conduct himself with on the weekdays, so that when the Sabbath day comes he may be able to receive the light of the additional soul properly. And so it is understood from the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (page 22b), in these words: for at the time the Shechinah is in exile, it is said of her, "and the dove found no rest" (Genesis 8:9), except on the Sabbath and festivals, at which time she is united with her husband, and how many additional souls descend with her to dwell among Israel - this is what is written (Exodus 31:16), "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to make the Sabbath throughout their generations" - happy is he who prepares for her a pleasant dwelling in his heart, and pleasant vessels in his limbs, and a pleasant wife in his soul - for whose sake the supernal Shechinah, which is the soul of all living, rests upon him - to this point. And certainly "a pleasant dwelling in his heart" is the purification of the heart's thoughts from evil reflections, and "pleasant vessels in his limbs," and so on, is that they not be blemished - and this preparation is certainly needed for all six days, just as it is needed for the sixth day, for if his limbs are blemished for six days, what he repairs on the sixth day will not suffice against what he blemished all the other days of the week. "And a pleasant wife in his soul" - this is the soul that is not blemished during the six weekdays, and through this he merits that the additional soul rest upon him - and this is what he says, "for whose sake the supernal Shechinah, which is the soul of all living, rests upon him," from which additional souls flow. And this is what is explained concerning "remember the Sabbath day," that it is an infinitive - that always, during the six weekdays, one must remember the holiness of the Sabbath and make these good preparations - a pleasant dwelling, and so on - so that he can receive the light of the Sabbath that shall rest upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:150: And so during the six days when the Shechinah is united with Torah scholars occupied with Torah (Parashat Kedoshim, page 81a), if they do not make these repairs mentioned for her, certainly she will not rest upon them, for she does not rest upon a blemished soul, as it is said (Leviticus 21:18), "whoever has a blemish shall not approach" - and therefore a person must always purify his thoughts and repair his deeds, and make "a pleasant dwelling" in his heart - to repair the heart in all the particulars we spoke of above concerning the repair of the heart in positive and negative aspects - and "pleasant vessels in his limbs" - that they not be blemished, and that there be in them the beauty and adornment of the fulfillment of the commandments. "A pleasant wife in his soul" - the essential repair of the soul is through Torah and the intent of prayer, for the soul is from the world of thought, and its repair, its adornment and beauty, is through the unifications a person performs through his thought - through this it shines, and he gains from this that when the Sabbath day comes, the purification of thought will be easy for him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:151: And all the holinesses a person practices on the Sabbath day will be easy for him to do on the weekdays, because on the Sabbath day all the days receive, each day, a portion of those holinesses - and it will not be hard for a person to practice what he did not do before, in a manner that if he did not repair anything during the six days of the week, and the Sabbath comes and he considers repentance, and wishes to perform all the holinesses practiced on it, all the holinesses he practiced on the Sabbath will help him, so that it be easy for him to draw those holinesses from the central point to all the days. But if the root, which is the point, is not properly repaired, the repair of each and every day, to illuminate it and sanctify it with the holiness of thought, speech, and the like, will be hard for him. And therefore, whoever comes to sanctify himself should first sanctify the six days, for the reason explained - and if he comes to repent on the Sabbath, since he did not remember his Maker during the working days, he should repair the Sabbath according to its law. And at the very least, on the eve of the Sabbath he should repair "a pleasant dwelling" in his heart - at least his thought, from the vanities of this world, and think of what we explained in chapter 2 of this Gate, that the Sabbath is a taste of the World to Come, as they said, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 3a), "whoever toils on Sabbath eve shall eat on the Sabbath," and so on. And so it is fitting that a person say in his heart, after he has prepared the needs of the Sabbath from eating and drinking - and what have I prepared for the world that is entirely Sabbath? And therefore it is fitting that on the sixth day he be solitary for part of the day, to examine what he did during the six days, so that he repent - and through this the days shall be included in the central point, which is the Sabbath, as explained there, and his soul shall be pleasant, through the intent of prayer as explained, and his limbs pleasant and repaired through repentant reflection at least - and through this there will be a preparation for the additional soul to rest upon him, so that he may be able to repent afterward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:152: Behold, we have spoken in general of the repair of the working days, that one must be a servant, and in general of the Sabbath day. But there are further preparations fitting to make on the sixth day in order to receive the Sabbath, and preparations fitting to make on the Sabbath itself, some of which are explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 204a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:153: And the essential thing a person must do on the sixth day, in his body, to acquire the holiness of the Sabbath and the additional soul, is immersion in forty se'ah [of water], in order to remove the garment of the weekday spirit and put on the spirit of the holiness of the Sabbath, which is the spirit that blows from Atika - for immersion is needed, so that perhaps that holy spirit rest upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:154: And among them is repentance in thought and deed - and the general rule is that alacrity, cleanliness, and purity all must be done on Sabbath eve, so that afterward the holiness, which is the holiness of the Sabbath, may rest - and through these preparations there will be a pleasant dwelling in his heart, pleasant limbs, and a pleasant soul - and if these are lacking, Heaven forfend, there is no repair at all and the holiness finds no place to rest. And he shall gain from this, that once the holiness of the Sabbath rests upon him properly, it will bring him to humility, fear of sin, piety, and the holy spirit, as mentioned in the teaching of Rabbi Pinchas (Avodah Zarah 20b) - for what causes one not to be humble, fearful of sin, and pious, with his inclination overpowering him? Because he has no soul that would overpower his inclination - and once a holy soul comes to him, it will certainly overpower him and he will be humble and fearful of sin, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:155: And according to the words of the Zohar in Parashat Vayakhel (page 204a), it appears to me that after he immerses, it is forbidden for him to occupy himself with performing work, but only with preparing the needs of the Sabbath. And correctly, after the immersion he should occupy himself with Torah until he receives the Sabbath, for the immersion is almost the receiving of the Sabbath - and this is his wording there: when the Sabbath enters, that holy people must wash themselves from the contact of the weekday - why? Because on weekdays another spirit goes about and roams and rests upon the people, and when a person wishes to leave that spirit and enter another, holy, supernal spirit, he must wash himself so that that holy supernal spirit may rest upon him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:156: And among the things needed for the holiness of thought, the essential one is the fundamental fear we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1 - that a person fear his Master, who is great and rules, the root and source of all worlds (Introduction to the Zohar, page 11b) - and it is explained, at the end of chapter 1, that a greater fear than this shall be drawn for a person when he considers the blessed and exalted Cause of all causes, who is the root and sustenance for all the worlds, without whose flow they have no existence - and included in this is man, who is a small world; the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him life through His flow, and were He to gather His spirit and soul to Himself, all flesh would perish together (cf. Job 34:14-15) - and concerning the Cause of all it is said (Nehemiah 9:6), "and You give life to them all," as they explained, of blessed memory, "and You give life, and You bring into being," and so on. And when a person stands in prayer or is occupied with Torah, and remembers this matter, that he stands before the Cause of all causes, that He is the root of all roots, and in Him stands the root of the life of his soul - he shall be ashamed to think of anything else but what he is speaking before Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:157: And this matter we mention in the Musaf prayer of Rosh Hashanah, in "You remember the deeds of the world and recall all the creatures of old," and so on - and my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, in interpreting the prayer, concerning what it says, "before You are revealed all hidden things and the multitude of secrets from the beginning" - that these are the secret of the supernal, hidden "clarities" [tzachtzachot] in the root of roots, through which roots all the created beings are figured in a single instant, and through those roots He watches over them - and His providence is not divided among the lower particulars, but rather He flows to them and watches over them through those united with Him. And the reality of these roots is revealed in Keter, Vav, and they are the primordial light, the pure light, the polished light [tzachtzach], as explained in the Tikkunim (page 135b), and my teacher, peace be upon him, explained in Sefer HaPardes, Gate of the Clarities (Gate 11, chapter 7), that the reality of these three lights is the three yuds in the Name of forty-three [Sag], Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, and there is an allusion in the Tikkunim (ibid., and page 115b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:158: And further, in the Tikkunim, in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 100a), it is explained that the reality of these three yuds are the root of nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, in these words: and happy is he who raises three prayers to Him with the three points of the property, from which are drawn three drops of the three supernal brains - for when a person emits seed from himself, these drops that are drawn from him are of the choicest of the choice of the brain, most select of all - so, in this manner, when the Holy One, blessed be He, causes to inherit in a person the three bonds, which are neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh, He gives him of His choicest of the choice, which are from the three "Yud-Yud" of the property, alluded to in the Name Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - and therefore He says of them (Deuteronomy 14:2), "and the LORD has chosen you to be for Him a treasured people [am segulah]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:159: And when a person considers that his neshamah, ru'ach, and nefesh are rooted above, it is fitting that he purify his thoughts and be ashamed to think of anything that is not His blessed service - all the more so to speak or do something against His will - because everything is revealed before Him, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:1-4), "O LORD, You have searched me and known me. You know my sitting down and my rising up, You understand my thought from afar," and so on, "for there is not a word on my tongue, but, behold, O LORD, You know it altogether" - and as he elaborates afterward concerning providence, "where shall I go from Your spirit," and so on, "if I ascend to heaven, You are there," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:160: And know that all the aspects mentioned concerning the root and source of all worlds are all revealed through the final measure, as Rashbi said in this teaching (Introduction to the Zohar, page 11b), "and to place one's will in that level called fear" - for all these aspects are attained through it, and His blessed providence toward us is through this measure, for it is the seal of the entire supernal Atzilut, and in it is the figure of our souls, as we elaborated in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 - and through it the greatness of the supernal Emanator and His dominion is revealed, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1. And it is this aspect of spiritual fear that Rashbi, peace be upon him, warns us of several times: "voice and speech in fear and love" (Tikkunei Zohar, page 132a), "a commandment in fear and love" (Tikkunei Zohar, page 50a), and many similar - for the intent is that a person know before whom he stands and whom he serves, and that he perform a commandment or occupy himself with Torah, and not perform the commandment as "a commandment of men, learned by rote," and so likewise concerning prayer and Torah - but rather that he cleave to his Maker properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:161: And from this fear shall be drawn for a person a subduing of his soul, to make himself small before the greatness of his Creator - and it is impossible for a person's soul to cleave to his God and draw holiness upon himself unless he subdues his soul before Him and accounts himself as nothing against His greatness and against all His goodness toward him - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Yitro, page 69a), in these words: because a matter from above, whether of holiness or of the Other Side, a person cannot draw a spirit from above downward and bring it near to himself except through fear, and he should direct his heart and his will with fear and a broken heart, and then the spirit from above and the necessary will shall be drawn below - and if he does not set his heart and his will with fear toward that side, his will cannot cleave to it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:162: And when a person wishes to cleave to his Maker in his occupation with Torah or in prayer, he should first think of the fear mentioned and subdue himself, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, will be found with him and cannot easily separate from him - for the Holy One, blessed be He, of Himself, is forever found and present, but from the side of the person himself, his soul, and the husks that separate between him and his God, time is needed until he subdues himself and separates the husk from himself and cleaves to holiness.
